title: Consumers’ Small Business Saturday Spending Rose 38% This Year, AmEx Reports

facts.fact: Spending at independent shops and restaurants on Small Business Saturday jumped 38% to an estimated $17.8 billion, according to American Express and the National Federation of Independent Business.
facts.quote: spending at independent shops and restaurants jumped 38% to an estimated $17.8 billion on Small Business Saturday

facts.fact: The estimated Small Business Saturday total was $15.4 billion in 2016, down from $16.2 billion in 2015, according to AmEx-supplied data.
facts.quote: a year in which the total slipped from $16.2 billion in 2015

facts.fact: The estimated Small Business Saturday spending total for 2014 was $14.3 billion, according to AmEx-supplied data.
American Express founded the Small Business Saturday promotion in 2010.
facts.quote: AmEx founded the Saturday-after-Thanksgiving promotion in 2010

facts.fact: AmEx declined to say how much billed business the Small Business Saturday event generated on its cards in any year.
facts.quote: AmEx declined to say how much billed business the event generated on its cards for each year

facts.fact: AmEx's survey found that 41% of respondents shopped small online on Small Business Saturday in 2018, up from 35% in 2017.
facts.quote: Our survey found that 41% reporting that they shopped small online on Small Business Saturday this year, an increase from 35% in 2017.

facts.fact: The Small Business Saturday promotion covers locally owned businesses in the United States and Puerto Rico.
facts.quote: to highlight locally owned businesses in the United States and Puerto Rico

facts.fact: AmEx's OptBlue program generated 1 million merchant accounts for AmEx in 2016.
facts.quote: The program generated 1 million merchant accounts for AmEx in 2016.

facts.fact: The Small Business Saturday spending estimates are an aggregate of consumer-reported average spend in AmEx-commissioned surveys and do not reflect actual receipts or sales.
facts.quote: It does not reflect actual receipts or sales.

facts.fact: The AmEx-commissioned surveys drew from a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults, with margins of error of plus or minus 2 to 5.47 percentage points at the 95% confidence level.
facts.quote: Survey respondents came from a nationally representative sample of U.S. adults. The surveys have margins of error ranging from plus or minus 2-to-5.47 percentage points at the 95% confidence level.
